summary: This bill amends Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964 to specify that the terms 'because of sex' and 'on the basis of sex' do not include discrimination based on gender identity.

scores.thoughts: The bill is a narrow clarification to Title VII of the Civil Rights Act regarding the definition of sex discrimination. It contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget authority.
The bill makes no changes to tax law, rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill addresses employment discrimination definitions and has no bearing on healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
No provisions relate to firearms, regulations, or Second Amendment issues.
The bill does not address immigration, visas, borders, or related enforcement.
No content touches on reproductive rights or abortion access.
The legislation has no connection to military funding, defense policy, or armed forces.
No environmental regulations, protections, or energy policy are involved.
The bill does not modify welfare programs, entitlements, or social services.
Although referred to the Education and Workforce Committee, the substance concerns Title VII employment law, not schools, funding, or education policy.
No references to controlled substances, enforcement, or decriminalization.
The bill does not address sentencing, policing, or criminal procedure.
No provisions on tariffs, trade agreements, or globalization.
The bill has no fiscal impact or implications for deficits or debt.

The bill explicitly states that 'because of sex' and 'on the basis of sex' under Title VII do not include gender identity. This directly narrows the scope of federal anti-discrimination protections for transgender individuals in employment, limiting legal protections on the basis of gender identity.
No provisions relate to foreign assistance or international aid.
The bill contains nothing about voting rights, election procedures, or voter access.
No technology, data privacy, or regulatory oversight provisions are present.
While Title VII affects employment, the bill does not engage with union rights, collective bargaining, or worker/employer power dynamics.
The bill narrows the definition of sex discrimination but does not address religious exemptions, conscience protections, or the balance between civil rights enforcement and religious liberty.
